notes: §1985:VI.6.26.4 GR5 puts SUBTRACT under the common paragraphs: "Additional rules and explanations relative to this statement are given under the appropriate paragraphs" (Scope of Statements, ROUNDED, ON SIZE ERROR, The Arithmetic Statements, Overlapping Operands, Multiple Results, CORRESPONDING). BindSubtract binds formats 1 and 2 and hands format 3 to BindSubtractCorresponding; none has an edition arm for these rules except the two 1985 needs: RoundingOf gives a bare ROUNDED the one 1985 rounding (§1985:VI.6.4.1 "increased by one in the low-order position whenever the most significant digit of the excess is greater than or equal to five"), and CheckComposite reads the edition's digit cap, 18 at 85 (§1985:VI.6.4.4 "must not contain more than 18 decimal digits"), over all operands in format 1 and without the GIVING items in format 2. EmitInPlace and EmitGiving evaluate the subtrahend sum once (Snapshot, when there are several receivers) and store left to right, so a later receiver's subscript sees an earlier result (§1985:VI.6.4.6); EmitArith with GuardedStore and StoreArith (CobolNum.TryStore) keeps a size-error receiver unchanged, stores the others, and runs the ON SIZE ERROR or NOT ON SIZE ERROR statements once after every store, which CorrespondingEmitter.Emit shares pair by pair (§1985:VI.6.4.2 "is not executed until all of the individual additions or subtractions are completed"); with no phrase the statement stores unchecked and goes on (no EC-SIZE checking exists at 85). Overlapping operands are undefined in 1985 (§1985:VI.6.4.5), so nothing is owed there. VisitStatementBlock refuses (COBOL2796) a SUBTRACT with a size-error phrase and no END-SUBTRACT where an imperative-statement is printed (§1985:IV.6.4.3). Probed at --std 85: 4850 into PIC 99PP ROUNDED gives 4900 and -5149 into S99PP gives -5100; -1.25 ROUNDED into S9V9 gives -1.3 and unrounded -1.54 gives -1.5; a PIC 99 COMP receiver takes the size error at 110; NOT ON SIZE ERROR alone is skipped on a size error and execution continues; SUBTRACT 1 FROM A T (A) updates T (2) after A becomes 2; a numeric-edited GIVING receiver is rounded then edited and keeps its content on size error; SUBTRACT CORR skips FILLER, a non-numeric partner, a REDEFINES entry and an OCCURS entry, matches a nested K under the same qualifier, leaves the overflowing pair unchanged and displays the size error after the other pairs are stored; a 20-digit format 1 composite and a 19-digit format 2 composite are refused (COBOL0805) while a 9(18) minuend GIVING a V99 item compiles. The witness runs ROUNDED on two receivers, GIVING with a rounded and an edited receiver, SIZE ERROR with one receiver unchanged and one stored, a subscript changed by an earlier result, CORRESPONDING with a size error, and END-SUBTRACT inside IF.

next.reason: 1985 GR5 points SUBTRACT to Scope of Statements, ROUNDED, ON SIZE ERROR, The Arithmetic Statements, Overlapping Operands, Multiple Results and CORRESPONDING; Overlapping Operands makes the result 'undefined' when a sending and receiving item share storage (§1985:VI.6.4.5). §2023:14.9.44.4 GR6 points to '14.6.13.2, Incompatible data; 14.7.4, ROUNDED phrase' and on to SIZE ERROR, CORRESPONDING and 14.7.7, and drops the overlap reference: §2023:14.7.7 GR4 now carries multiple results and makes 'the results contained in the receiving operands for all arithmetic statements ... defined regardless of whether any of the sending operands share storage', which §2023:14.6.10 defers to because the statement rules 'provide for a specific result'. An overlapping SUBTRACT, undefined in 1985, has a defined result in 2023, and the incompatible-data rules are newly attached; the referenced requirement set differs.
